name: Easing graph draw
looks: A position-over-time graph draws a straight line labelled as the mechanical, wrong way, then redraws itself as an S-curve with a check mark. Beneath it, a row of small boxes marches along a timeline, bunching and spreading to match whichever curve is showing, so the shape and its effect are visible together.
build: Draw the curve on one 2D canvas from the master clock with a progressive lineTo reveal up to the current time. Drive the marching boxes' x positions with the same ease function the graph is showing, so the picture and the maths are literally the same number, and reserve the accent colour for the correct curve.
sound: A quiet bed with a tick per box.
prompt: Draw a simple curve twice: once as a flat, mechanical line marked as the wrong approach, then again as an eased curve marked as the right one, with a row of small marching elements beneath that bunch and spread to match whichever curve is live. Use this before/after pairing for any contrast between a rough and a refined version of growth, cost, speed or load time.
